title: Shared HTTP helpers and errors
description: Set currentAccessToken from the OAuth token response. Helpers throw structured errors and expose Retry-After. Refresh expired tokens through OAuth, obtain new consent for scope changes, and retry only transient failures; do not blindly retry permission or validation errors.

title: OAuth PKCE: connect, verify the callback, exchange code
description: Use a registered redirect URI exactly. Persist state, verifier and redirect URI through the round trip, validate state before exchanging, and clear the pending attempt after success. On Android, open the authorization URL in the system browser and handle your registered app link/custom scheme; localhost is for desktop loopback listeners. Confidential client secrets belong only on a server. The preserved Node example shows a loopback listener.
kotlin:
import java.security.SecureRandom
import java.security.MessageDigest
import java.util.Base64
import android.net.Uri

val clientId = "YOUR_CLIENT_ID"
val redirectUri = "yourapp://oauth/callback" // Register exactly this URI first.
fun randomUrlToken(): String = Base64.getUrlEncoder().withoutPadding().encodeToString(
    ByteArray(32).also { SecureRandom().nextBytes(it) })
val verifier = randomUrlToken()
val state = randomUrlToken()
val challenge = Base64.getUrlEncoder().withoutPadding().encodeToString(
    MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA-256").digest(verifier.toByteArray(Charsets.US_ASCII)))
val authorizeUrl = "https://api.pocketpass.xyz/auth/v1/oauth/authorize?" + form(mapOf(
    "client_id" to clientId, "redirect_uri" to redirectUri, "response_type" to "code",
    "scope" to "openid", "state" to state, "code_challenge" to challenge, "code_challenge_method" to "S256"))
// Persist verifier/state/redirectUri privately, then launch authorizeUrl in the system browser.

// In your redirect handler, restore the persisted values first:
fun finishLogin(callbackUrl: String, expectedState: String, savedVerifier: String): JSONObject {
    val callback = Uri.parse(callbackUrl)
    val expected = Uri.parse(redirectUri)
    require(callback.scheme == expected.scheme && callback.authority == expected.authority && callback.path == expected.path)
    require(callback.getQueryParameter("state") == expectedState) { "Invalid OAuth state" }
    require(callback.getQueryParameter("error") == null) { "Authorization rejected" }
    val code = requireNotNull(callback.getQueryParameter("code"))
    return requestJson("https://api.pocketpass.xyz/auth/v1/oauth/token", form(mapOf(
        "grant_type" to "authorization_code", "client_id" to clientId, "code" to code,
        "redirect_uri" to redirectUri, "code_verifier" to savedVerifier)), "application/x-www-form-urlencoded")
}
// Run exchange on an IO thread; securely store returned tokens and clear pending state.

title: Refresh, disconnect and confidential clients
description: Serialize refreshes for each user and replace both stored tokens after a successful refresh. Never embed a confidential-client secret in a browser or mobile app. Confidential clients authenticate token requests with HTTP Basic from their trusted server; see the server-side example.

title: Pagination and incremental sync
description: Treat cursors as opaque. Use the documented timestamp filters for incremental messages/conversations/encounters. Realtime is an invalidation signal: refetch through the scoped API and discard private caches when access is lost.

title: Realtime presence and sorted friend topics
description: These snippets construct the raw Phoenix join for your WebSocket client; they are not complete transport implementations. Use the documented WebSocket URL and a unique ref for each frame, maintain Phoenix heartbeats, handle presence_state/presence_diff, and rejoin after reconnecting. Set presence.enabled explicitly. Never log the access token. The original SDK example is preserved below.

title: Read last-seen time
description: Requires friends:read plus presence:read. The timestamp is not a replacement for live Presence. An absent field means it is not available to this request; null means no activity was recorded. Display a localized time or relative age without claiming the friend is currently online.

title: Draw, save a draft, publish and react
description: Use the drawing format below with boards.publish or boards.draw_branding. Save drafts explicitly with boards.save_draft; preserve revisions when conflict is true. Keep publication requests and operation IDs after errors. Publishing is always a user action, never an automatic result of reconnecting.
kotlin:
val drawing = JSONObject("""{"version":1,"width":800,"height":600,"strokes":[
  {"pen":"pixel","color":"#222222","size":4,"points":[[10,10],[40,30]]}]}""")
val draft = JSONObject().put("board_id", boardId)
    .put("draft_id", java.util.UUID.randomUUID().toString())
    .put("revision_id", java.util.UUID.randomUUID().toString())
    .put("payload", JSONObject().put("body", "Hello everyone!").put("drawing", drawing))
    .put("operation_id", java.util.UUID.randomUUID().toString())
val saved = api("boards.save_draft", draft)
// Preserve both versions when conflict is true. Publish only after the user's action:
val pending = JSONObject().put("board_id", boardId).put("body", "Hello everyone!").put("drawing", drawing)
    .put("operation_id", java.util.UUID.randomUUID().toString())
val published = api("boards.publish", pending)
val reaction = JSONObject().put("board_id", boardId).put("post_id", published.getString("id"))
    .put("yeah", true).put("operation_id", java.util.UUID.randomUUID().toString())
// Send only when the user presses Yeah:
api("boards.react", reaction)

title: Block accounts and block incoming messages
description: These are separate settings. Account blocking removes the friendship; unblocking does not restore it. Block Messages prevents incoming DMs and new invitations/group additions without leaving existing groups or boards.
kotlin:
val block = JSONObject().put("user_id", selectedUserId).put("blocked", true)
    .put("operation_id", java.util.UUID.randomUUID().toString())
api("blocks.set", block) // Requires blocks:write.
val privacy = JSONObject().put("block_messages", true)
    .put("operation_id", java.util.UUID.randomUUID().toString())
api("privacy.set", privacy) // Requires privacy:write.

title: Download, sign and upload message media
description: Use the existing media limits and allowed MIME types from the Media reference. Upload bytes first, then send the message with its attachment path. On retries reuse the same path and operation ID; do not blindly overwrite a conflicting object. Avatar signing uses profile:read; message media uses the relevant messaging scope.

title: Server-side confidential-client token exchange
description: Server only. Retrieve the secret from your secret store. Validate callback state and use the saved PKCE verifier before running this exchange. Do not put the secret in a browser, APK or iOS app.

title: Realtime broadcast and reconnection
description: Raw frames for your WebSocket transport. Use the publishable key from developer.pocketpass.xyz/config.js in the connection URL, and the user access token in the join payload. Maintain heartbeats and merge presence_state/presence_diff with your library. On disconnect, reconnect and rejoin with the current token, then refetch to recover missed events.
